title: Bluetooth speaker or headphones connected but no sound or missing from output list
symptoms: Settings shows the Bluetooth speaker or headphones as Connected, but no sound comes out
Sound keeps playing from the PC speakers instead of the Bluetooth device
The device is missing from the Sound output list, or shows as Disconnected in the Playback tab
Settings shows only 'Connected' instead of 'Connected voice, music' / 'Audio, Voice'
causes: Windows is still sending audio to another output device
The stereo (A2DP) audio endpoint was not created or is in a disconnected state after pairing
The pairing record or Bluetooth driver is in a bad state after an update
The device does not support the A2DP stereo audio profile

signals: A Bluetooth device is connected, but no matching audio endpoint is active
The Bluetooth audio endpoint exists but is not the default playback device
The Bluetooth audio endpoint shows as disconnected or not present while the device shows as connected

fixes.title: Select the Bluetooth device as the output device
steps: Select the Sound icon in the taskbar and pick the Bluetooth device from the output list.
Or open Settings > System > Sound and choose the Bluetooth device under Output.
If it is not listed, open Settings > System > Sound > More sound settings > Playback tab.
If the Bluetooth device (usually 'Headphones' or 'Speakers', not 'Headset') shows as Disconnected, right-click it and select Connect.
Right-click the Bluetooth device and select Set as Default Device.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft support article, step 'Check the default output device'
Microsoft Q&A answer by Independent Advisor, 100+ people found it helpful (not marked accepted)

fixes.title: Remove the device and pair it again
steps: Open Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Devices.
Select More options (...) next to the speaker or headphones and choose Remove device.
Turn Bluetooth off, wait about 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
Put the speaker or headphones in pairing mode and select Add device to pair it again.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft support article, steps 'Unpair and re-pair' and 'Toggle Bluetooth'
Official Microsoft support article, step 5 remove and re-add the device
Microsoft Q&A answer by Independent Advisor, 100+ people found it helpful; first step is remove and pair again

fixes.title: Run the Bluetooth troubleshooter
steps: Windows 11: open the Get Help app and run the Bluetooth troubleshooter, or go to Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters and select Run next to Bluetooth.
Windows 10: go to Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot > Additional troubleshooters and run Bluetooth.
Follow the on-screen instructions.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft support article
Official Microsoft support article, first step
Microsoft Q&A community answer, 70+ people found it helpful

fixes.title: Update the Bluetooth adapter driver
steps: Open Device Manager and expand Bluetooth.
Right-click the Bluetooth adapter (often named with 'Wireless Bluetooth' or 'radio') and select Update driver > Search automatically for drivers.
If Windows finds nothing, install the latest Bluetooth driver from the PC or motherboard manufacturer's support page.
Restart the PC.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft support article, step 'Update drivers'
Official Microsoft support article, steps 7-8
Microsoft Q&A community answer, 70+ people found it helpful (driver update / install from PC maker)

title: Bluetooth headphones sound muffled or mono when the microphone is in use
symptoms: Music or game audio becomes muffled, tinny or mono when a call, Discord, Teams or a game with voice chat starts
Audio sounds fine until an app opens the microphone
Two entries appear for the headset: 'Headphones' (Stereo) and 'Headset' (Hands-Free)
causes: When an app uses the headset microphone, Windows switches the headset from the stereo profile (A2DP) to the Hands-Free profile (HFP), which carries mono, low-bitrate audio
Bluetooth Classic cannot use the headset microphone and the stereo profile at the same time

signals: The Hands-Free (Headset) endpoint of a Bluetooth device is the active or default communication device
Audio quality drops at the same time an app opens the Bluetooth headset microphone

fixes.title: Turn off Hands-free Telephony for the headset (headset mic stops working)
steps: Know the trade-off first: the headset microphone will stop working. Use the PC's built-in microphone or another microphone for calls.
Open Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Devices and select More devices and printer settings (Windows 10: Control Panel > Devices and Printers).
Right-click the headset and select Properties.
Open the Services tab and clear the Hands-free Telephony check box.
Select Apply, then OK.
In Settings > System > Sound, set Input to another microphone.
If the setting turns back on after a reboot, reconnect or Windows update, repeat these steps. To undo, select the check box again.

sources.signal: Microsoft Q&A: asker confirms unchecking Hands-free Telephony fixes quality but removes the mic; advisor answer (3 helpful) explains the limitation and recommends another mic
Microsoft Q&A advisor answer, 5 people found it helpful; not accepted
Three users report that unchecking Handsfree Telephony in the Services tab fixes the audio; two report it resets after a reboot or reconnect

title: Bluetooth audio stutters or drops out while Wi-Fi is in use
symptoms: Bluetooth audio crackles, skips or cuts out
Dropouts are worse during downloads, streaming or online games
Turning off Wi-Fi makes the Bluetooth audio smooth
causes: Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi share the same radio band and, on combo Wi-Fi/Bluetooth cards, the same antenna

signals: A Bluetooth audio device is active while the Wi-Fi connection uses the 2.4 GHz band

fixes.title: Connect the PC to a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network
steps: Select the Wi-Fi icon in the taskbar and open the Wi-Fi network list.
Connect to your router's 5 GHz network if it has one (often named with '5G').
To check the band, open Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > the network's properties and look at Network band.
If you cannot use 5 GHz, use a wired Ethernet connection or test with Wi-Fi turned off to confirm the cause.

sources.signal: Official Intel support article: recommends 5 GHz Wi-Fi to avoid interference between Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
Intel Customer Support technician reply on Bluetooth audio stutter: switch Wi-Fi to 5 GHz (no asker confirmation shown)

title: Bluetooth volume is too low or the volume controls do not work
symptoms: Bluetooth speaker or headphones are quiet even at 100% volume in Windows
The Windows volume slider does not change the Bluetooth device volume
Volume jumps or resets when the device reconnects
causes: Windows Absolute Volume links the Windows slider to the device's own volume, and some devices handle it badly
A Windows update changed how Absolute Volume works with the device

signals: A Bluetooth audio device is connected and the DisableAbsoluteVolume value under HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Bluetooth\Audio\AVRCP\CT is missing or 0

fixes.title: Remove the device and pair it again
steps: Open Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Devices.
Select More options (...) next to the device and choose Remove device.
Pair the device again, then set the volume in Windows and on the device.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft support article, remove and re-add the device
Microsoft Q&A volume thread: two commenters report removing and re-adding the device fixed it (one says volume later reverted)

fixes.title: Turn off Bluetooth Absolute Volume (registry)
steps: Create a restore point first. This is a registry change.
Open PowerShell or Command Prompt as administrator.
Run: reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Bluetooth\Audio\AVRCP\CT /v DisableAbsoluteVolume /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
Restart the PC.
After this, the Windows slider and the device's own volume buttons work separately. Turn up the volume on the device itself.
To undo, run the same command with /d 0 and restart. Some users report results got worse (quieter, or the headphones stopped working), so undo it if that happens.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft support article giving this exact reg add command (seen in search index; direct fetch on 2026-10-28 redirected to the Windows help landing page)
Microsoft Q&A answer by Microsoft staff, 20+ people found it helpful; comments report mixed results

title: No sound on the PC because the speaker or headphones are also connected to a phone
symptoms: The speaker or headphones are connected to the PC and a phone at the same time
The PC shows the device as connected, but sound plays from the phone or nothing plays
PC audio stops after a phone call or notification and does not come back
causes: In a multipoint connection, only one device plays audio at a time, usually the one that played last
The phone keeps the audio link after a call or notification

signals: A Bluetooth audio device is connected, but no audio stream reaches it while it is also paired to another device

fixes.title: Stop playback on the phone, then restart playback on the PC
steps: Pause or stop music, video and calls on the phone, and close its media app.
On the PC, pause playback and start it again.
If sound still does not play, turn off Bluetooth on the phone or disconnect the speaker from the phone.
If the device has a companion app, check that its multipoint setting (for example 'Connect to 2 devices simultaneously') is on.

sources.signal: Official Sony help guide: audio plays from the last-used device; stop playback on the first device to hear the second
Microsoft Q&A (MVP moderator replied): asker reports PC audio stays silent after phone use until playback is paused and restarted
